titulo: Eye, brain, and hand: inside a VLA
lead: Every VLA has three parts: one that sees, one that understands, and one that turns the decision into movement. The movement part is where models differ the most, and where the clock gets tight: the arm waits for a command every few milliseconds.
objetivo: explain the path from image + sentence → actions and why action chunking and flow matching exist.

aprende.t: The three parts: visual encoder, backbone, and action head
Three ways to generate action: bins, FAST, and flow matching
Why the model returns a piece of actions (chunk)
The slow/fast hierarchy: S2, S1, and S0

hero_alt: Close-up of the wrist camera and the gripper of a robotic arm about to pick up a cup.

secoes.titulo: The path from camera to motor
secoes.sub: Scroll the page: each step lights up a part of the diagram.

nos.detalhe: Turns each image into a sequence of vectors that the rest of the model understands. It usually comes ready-made from a pretrained VLM.

A VLM that takes the image tokens, the instruction, and the robot's state. 2026 examples: GR00T N1.7 uses Cosmos-Reason2-2B; RDT2 uses Qwen2.5-VL-7B. This is where the "understands" in the course title comes from.

Turns the backbone's decision into motor numbers. You can pick values from a list (bins), write the compressed trajectory as tokens (FAST), or generate the continuous action with flow matching or diffusion.

nos.sub: the piece that goes to the motor

itens.t: The robot executes while the model thinks

nos.detalhe: Instead of one action at a time, the model returns a chunk of N actions. The controller executes that chunk while the model computes the next one.

secoes.legenda: In most 2026 VLAs the backbone is a pretrained VLM, and what changes from one model to another is the action head.

rolagem_fim.texto: The camera becomes tokens, the backbone combines them with the sentence and the state, the action head returns a chunk of actions, and the motor executes while the next chunk is computed.

secoes.titulo: Three ways to generate the action
secoes.sub: Click each one. The difference is speed and precision.

texto: Each joint has its range of motion divided into little boxes (bins), and the model picks a box the way it would pick a word. Models like OpenVLA (7B, Jun/2024) follow this idea.
It's simple, but it gives one action at a time, and precision is limited by the size of the box.
Physical Intelligence's FAST tokenization applies a transform (DCT) and compression (BPE) to a piece of the trajectory, which becomes a few tokens. According to PI, it trains 5 times faster.
In May/2026, Ai2's MolmoAct 2 published an open reimplementation of the FAST tokenizer, with open data.
A part of the model dedicated to action (the action expert) starts from noise and pushes it toward the right action, in continuous values. This is the π0 approach.

Diffusion is a close relative: GR00T uses a 32-layer DiT (diffusion transformer), and the model from Boston Dynamics and TRI controls the entire Atlas at 30 Hz with a diffusion transformer and flow matching (Aug/2025).

exemplo.texto: Fine, fast movement: continuous action in chunks. Step-by-step reasoning: tokens.

texto: A big model thinks slowly; a motor wants fast commands. The solution is to stack systems. In Figure's Helix (Feb/2025), S2 is a VLM at 7–9 Hz and S1 is a policy at 200 Hz.
Helix 02 (Jan/2026) added S0: a 10M-parameter whole-body controller at 1 kHz, which replaces 109,504 lines of C++.

secoes.sub: A ten-line script that answers: is there time for the model to think before the chunk runs out?

blocos.conteudo:
# orcamento.py: how much time each chunk of actions covers
hz = 50            # control frequency (commands per second)
chunk = 25         # actions the model returns at once
inferencia_ms = 180  # time for the model to generate a chunk

periodo_ms = 1000 / hz
dura_chunk_ms = chunk * periodo_ms
acoes_na_espera = inferencia_ms / periodo_ms

print(f"control period: {periodo_ms:.0f} ms")
print(f"a chunk of {chunk} actions covers: {dura_chunk_ms:.0f} ms")
print(f"actions that go by while the model thinks: {acoes_na_espera:.0f}")
print("is there time to think before the chunk runs out?", "yes" if inferencia_ms < dura_chunk_ms else "no")

abas.html:
$ python3 orcamento.py
control period: 20 ms
a chunk of 25 actions covers: 500 ms
actions that go by while the model thinks: 9
is there time to think before the chunk runs out? yes

The 180 ms is the time of one MolmoAct 2 action call as reported by Ai2 (May/2026). On your robot, measure yours.

• Forgetting the wait: while the model computes, the robot keeps moving. If the chunk runs out first, the arm stops or repeats the last action.
  • Mixing up Hz and ms: 50 Hz is 50 commands per second, one every 20 ms.

secoes.sub: Do the math before running the script, then check it.

exercicios.texto: Copy orcamento.py, run it, and check that the output matches the one in the box.
exercicios.pronto: your terminal shows 20 ms, 500 ms, 9, and "yes".

exercicios.texto: Change chunk to 8 and keep 50 Hz and 180 ms. Before running, write down on paper: how much the chunk covers, how many actions go by during the wait, and whether there is enough time.
exercicios.pronto: your paper and your terminal say the same thing: 160 ms, 9 actions, and "no" (the chunk ends before the next inference).

exercicios.titulo: E3 · The smallest chunk that works
exercicios.texto: Still at 50 Hz and 180 ms, find the smallest chunk that gives enough time.
exercicios.pronto: you got to 10 actions (200 ms, greater than 180 ms) and you can explain why 9 is not enough.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: A controller at 50 Hz with a chunk of 25 actions. How long does the chunk cover?
perguntas.explica: 50 Hz = one command every 20 ms. 25 × 20 ms = 500 ms. The common mistake is multiplying 25 by 50.

opcoes: So the model can be smaller.
So the robot has actions to execute while the model, slower than the motor, computes the next ones.
Because the motor only accepts lists.
perguntas.explica: The large model takes hundreds of milliseconds; the motor wants a command every few milliseconds. The chunk covers that gap.

perguntas.p: Which action head generates the action as a continuous value, starting from noise?
perguntas.explica: Flow matching (π0) and diffusion (GR00T's DiT) generate continuous values. Bins picks from a list; FAST writes the compressed trajectory as tokens.

perguntas.p: In Helix 02, what does S0 do?
opcoes: Understands the user's sentence at 7–9 Hz.
Controls the whole body at 1 kHz, with 10M parameters.
perguntas.explica: S2 understands slowly, S1 decides the joint targets at 200 Hz, and S0 controls the whole body at 1 kHz. Each layer at its own pace.

itens.texto: Visual encoder, backbone (a VLM), and action head.

itens.t: The hand is where it changes
itens.texto: Bins, FAST, or flow matching/diffusion: a list, compressed tokens, or continuous.
A chunk of N actions at 50 Hz covers N × 20 ms, and it has to last longer than the inference.
